summary: Grays Harbor County lookout site on a DNR parcel; sources disagree on the structure and dates, but it was gone by 1970 and no standing structure is described.

facts.design: 10 x 10 ft wood-frame portable ground house (Willhite, Forest Lookouts); firelookout.com describes an L-5 cab
facts.status_note: Gone by 1970; no source describes a structure at the site today

events.note: Register says a cabin was built here in 1942; Willhite says the Kresek inventory suggests use in 1942
firelookout.com: L-5 cab moved to the end of the ridge two miles southeast (date marked with a question mark for the original cab)
Register says a trailer was set up on the site
Gone by 1970 per the register, firelookout.com and Willhite's inventory notes
Registered January 13, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: register: cabin built 1942, trailer set up 1964, both gone by 1970
evidence.quote: A cabin built here in 1942 and in 1964 a trailer was set up. These were gone by 1970.

evidence.quote: Not dated: 10 x 10 wood frame portable ground house on the Quinault Ranger District.

evidence.quote: The Kresek lookout inventory suggests use in 1942 and removal by 1970.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: cabin 1942 and trailer 1964. Firelookout.com: an L-5 cab from the 1950s (dated with a question mark), moved in 1958. Forest Lookouts: an undated portable ground house. Willhite: the Kresek inventory suggests use in 1942. The story reports both accounts and does not choose one.

Register and firelookout.com name Washington Division of Forestry/DNR; Willhite calls the landowner DNR and says the parcel is inside the National Forest; Forest Lookouts files it under Olympic National Forest. The story uses the register's agency name.

sources.title: Humptulips Ridge Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'unknown' left as is: no source states public access. Willhite's route directions were left out on purpose (gone site on DNR land). Firelookout.com also mentions a separate WWII Aircraft Warning Service site called Humptulips west of Highway 101; it is not this lookout and is not used. No staffing sources found.
